g.text: waiting on you: a question, plan, permission prompt or dialog
idle: at the prompt, your turn
Claude Code reports a shell state
in ctx's tmux: Enter brings it to the left pane
not running: Enter resumes it in a new window
on another host: Enter resumes it there over ssh
running in another terminal: can't be adopted; quit it there,
on another host: open it there
its number: Alt+1…9 opens it from any pane of the ctx session
time in this state (live), or since it was last active (ended)
Windows-native Claude Code, then its host (cw·devbox)
a question has waited this long
a workstream header (w): this repo + branch on any host; m
a pool job launched by the session above (indented under it):
its brief, how it ended, its turns. It has no number: Alt+N
a job's estimated local cost (energy); the Spend screen ($)
under a waiting row: what it's waiting on — the question it
asked, or the dialog it has up
the header: how many sessions wait on you (and how many are
the header's second line: what has gone since midnight here —
cloud (with the accounts in brackets), and SAINT's local
energy estimate (— when it has none)
the detail pane's SPEND section: what this session's own turns
cost at Bedrock on-demand rates (`bedrock-spend` has the bill)
what it ran on the local box, estimated from its energy use
the header: what's left of the month's budget (the real bill,
from bedrock-spend); the line turns yellow at 75% used, red at
the Spend screen: today, 7 and 30 days by account and model,
queued: waiting for its host to pick it up
delivered: the agent is working on it
failed: the reason is shown; send it again
